You know $f(30)$ and you want to find $f(40)$. How can you choose $x$ and $y$ in the equation $f(xy) = \frac{f(x)}{y}$ to turn 30 into 40?
Fine, be a robot. If I set $x=30$, then $xy$ has to be 40. So $30y = 40$. That means $y = 4/3$. Now what?

That's the right approach for setting up the variables. Now, substitute those values ($x=30$ and $y=4/3$) back into the original functional equation $f(xy) = \frac{f(x)}{y}$. What does the equation look like once you plug those in?
It becomes $f(40) = f(30) / (4/3)$. And I know $f(30) = 20$. So it's $20 / (4/3)$. I'll just calculate that myself. Thanks I guess.
You've set up the calculation perfectly. Once you perform that division, you'll have your result. Good luck with the rest of your quiz!
